title: U.S. House · California's 38th District
area: Southeast Los Angeles County and San Gabriel Valley, including El Monte, Baldwin Park, West Covina, and Whittier.

context.text: This is an open seat with no incumbent in the race, following California's 2025 congressional redistricting (Proposition 50). California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary; in the June 2, 2026 primary, Hilda Solis (D) placed first with 47.6% and Pedro Casas (R) placed second, advancing to the November general election.

candidates.name: Hilda Solis
candidates.currentRole: Los Angeles County Supervisor, District 1 (2014–2026); did not seek re-election to that seat in 2026

summary.text: Hilda Solis is a member of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors who previously represented California's 32nd Congressional District from 2001 to 2009 and served as U.S. Secretary of Labor from 2009 to 2013. She is running for this newly drawn open seat.

background.text: Born in Los Angeles, California; earned a bachelor's degree from California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, and a Master of Public Administration from the University of Southern California.
Worked in the Carter White House Office of Hispanic Affairs and as a management analyst in the civil rights division of the federal Office of Management and Budget.
Served in the California State Assembly (1992–1994) and California State Senate (1994–2001), then represented California's 32nd Congressional District from 2001 to 2009.

Served as U.S. Secretary of Labor under President Barack Obama from 2009 to 2013, then was elected to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors in 2014, where she has served since; she did not run for re-election to that seat in 2026.

summary.text: Pedro 'Antonio' Casas is a retired U.S. Army colonel and clinical/forensic/aero-medical psychologist running as a Republican for this open seat, describing himself as a native of the district.

background.text: Identifies as Dr. Pedro 'Antonio' Casas, Ph.D., a retired Colonel in the U.S. Army and a clinical, forensic, and aero-medical psychologist.
Says he grew up in the 38th Congressional District, contrasting himself with opponents he describes as not being from the area.
background.quote: As the only candidate, regardless of political party, I originate from the very heart of the 38th Congressional District. Unlike others, I am not an outsider; I understand and can genuinely represent what I have grown up knowing.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists education standards, combating fentanyl trafficking, criminal-justice policy, border security, and addressing inflation and the cost of housing, food, and utilities as priorities, along with tax cuts and reduced business regulation.

positions.summary: Says he will work to secure the southern border and implement immigration reforms prioritizing national security.
positions.quote: I will work to secure our southern border and implement immigration reforms that prioritize national security.

positions.summary: Proposes tax cuts and reducing regulation on small businesses to stimulate economic growth, rather than raising taxes.
positions.quote: To stimulate economic growth, I propose tax cuts, reduction of bureaucratic red tape and excessive regulations on small businesses, allowing the free market to recalibrate itself.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in California, 2026

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No current campaign-issues page or public statements were found for Solis beyond her official biography, so no priorities/positions are cited for her; her extensive prior record as a member of Congress (2001–2009) and Secretary of Labor is not detailed here since it predates the 'record is what an officeholder did in office' scope available from the sources checked.
